summary: Interpreted the repaired live-cluster receipt and closed the constructor question's fixture limitation. Receipt ea93eea3cc08408ab3cd208ca9b1e5ca evaluated all five comparisons: the follower restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs never finished NewRaft within the window (violated, witness index 1), while the same stores restarted without the feature returned (holds, index 3), stayed at the snapshot index (applied_at_snapshot holds, index 3), faced a replay demand larger than the capacity observed on that same node (replay_exceeds_channel holds with capacity 128, index 3) and left the other two voters with a quorum (holds, index 2). Since the gap was produced by ordinary operations — bootstrap, election, five applies, a user snapshot at index 7, 250 further committed entries giving a staged commit index of 257, and a graceful shutdown — the earlier "no live node produced the gap" limitation is resolved, and the stall fact gained this receipt as an execution. The experiment-level interpretation is violated/asserted with those indices and the mechanism traced through restoreFromCommittedLogs → processLogs → fsmMutateCh with runFSM started after the constructor returns; the question-level account is explained/asserted with a joint history across its three receipts and with the remaining limits made explicit (the live restart used MaxAppendEntries 1, so at the default 64 the required gap of 8193 entries sits just above the default SnapshotThreshold and depends on snapshot delay or failure; the 5 s window with permanence argued from source; in-memory stores, graceful shutdown, and an abandoned stalled constructor with no supervision). Incomplete: a long-run window over the divergence chain, and the user Restore and term-changing truncation repair paths.
